manifest.name: @hayward/workspace
manifest.author: Hayward
manifest.description: Read, write, and edit files in the agent's workspace, and run shell commands over them like ls, grep, and find.

tools.name: bash_run
tools.description: Run a shell command line against the workspace. Available: ls, cat, head, tail, wc, sort, uniq, cut, nl, mv, cp, touch, env (real coreutils, so standard flags like 'ls -la', 'head -n 20' work); grep (ripgrep-backed: -i, -n, -v, -c, -l, -r, -w, -F, -E); find (-name, -iname, -path, -type f|d, -maxdepth, -mindepth, -not); sed ('s///'); plus cd, pwd, echo, mkdir, rm, true, false. Globs ('*', '?', '[...]'), pipelines ('|'), ';'/'&&'/'||' sequencing, and '>'/'>>' redirection all work — except that head, tail, wc, sort, uniq, cut, nl, mv, cp and touch run only as standalone commands, not inside a pipeline or a redirect. Returns combined stdout+stderr as 'output', the last command's exit code, and the resulting cwd — pass that back as 'cwd' to persist a 'cd'.

command.description: The shell command line to run, e.g. "cat src/main.rs | grep TODO".

cwd.description: Workspace-relative working directory to run in. Defaults to the workspace root ('.'). Pass back a previous call's 'cwd' result to persist a 'cd'.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file in full, returning its contents as JSON. Fails on non-UTF-8/binary content rather than mangling it.

cwd.description: Directory 'path' is relative to. Defaults to the workspace root ('.').

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write text to a file, overwriting it if it exists. Creates missing parent directories first. Prefer this over an echo/redirect in bash_run, which mangles quoting and multi-line content.

content.description: Text to write, replacing any existing content.

cwd.description: Directory 'path' is relative to. Defaults to the workspace root ('.').

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace one exact occurrence of old_string with new_string. Fails if old_string is missing or appears more than once — supply enough surrounding context to make the match unique. Prefer this over sed in bash_run, which has no uniqueness check and will silently change the wrong line.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace; must occur exactly once in the file.

cwd.description: Directory 'path' is relative to. Defaults to the workspace root ('.').
